### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **1** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 35b178bd0a9090aaccf9c767b0c6abf1067eff01` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

Still `in_progress`: Test Core 1–8, Test UI 1–16, Type Check UI, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · workspace. No failure. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; this record judges the tree.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set: none moves.** No schema, key, enum value, route or runtime file is in the diff. Both changesets and the PR body declare `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` — right.
- **Skills text (integration-recipes.md).** The "Not yet" OAuth bullet on `main` ("no server runs the grant yet … marked blocked") is false on `main` today: `connector-rest-plugin.ts:84`, `connector-openapi-plugin.ts:96` and `connector-mcp-plugin.ts:104` each register `{ credentialHandle: true }`, and `plugin.ts` (`oauth2NotServableReason`, the `app-credential` branch at the materialization site) holds a grant-bearing instance degraded only when the provider does not apply the handle, when an `oauth2` instance lacks endpoints it cannot discover, or when an endpoint is not https. Rewriting the bullet as recipe 6 is the right derived judgment; every sentence of recipe 6 checked against the spec and the code is listed under ④.
- **Skills text (SKILL.md loader-gap line).** Dropping "OAuth" — right: the `openapi` loader reads `components.securitySchemes` including `oauth2` (`openapi-connector.ts:134-139, 390`) and only uses `security` to decide where the token is not sent (connectors.mdx § Grant-bearing kinds). Keeping "request signing" unqualified — wrong in the same way "OAuth" was: `ConnectorSigningSchemeSchema` serves `aliyun-acs3-hmac-sha256`, `tencentcloud-tc3-hmac-sha256` and `alipay-v3` on `openapi` / `rest` (the recipes file's own Holds bullet teaches this), so an AI author whose vendor is Alibaba Cloud, Tencent Cloud or Alipay is told by SKILL.md that signing is "a gap named against its platform card, never a reason to write code". The qualified truth (WeChat Pay alone) lives in the recipes file's "Not yet", which the line's own pointer reaches — should-fix, not must-fix (see ④ S1).
- **Eval 1 rubric.** `must_contain` gains `oauth2`, `authorization_code`, `/connection` and drops `blocked`; `must_not_contain` gains `blocked on outbound OAuth`. A "still blocked" answer cannot pass: it would have to name the connect route `/connection` while not saying "blocked on outbound OAuth", and the rubric's `expected_output` names the connect flow as the served path. A right answer is not failed: every `must_contain` token appears in `expected_output`; `token:` does not match `tokenUrl` (no colon follows `token` there) and `clientSecret:` does not match the rubric's own "no inline `clientSecret`,"; "Swagger 2.0" and the polled-webhook gap stay. Right.
- **Lint explanation string (`flow-credential-literal`, what `os explain` / `os lint` prints).** "…obtains per dispatch through the built-in `rest`, `openapi` and `mcp` providers (an `authorization_code` instance once an administrator connects it); on a provider that does not ask the credential handle such an instance is held degraded and calls no upstream" — each clause holds against `plugin.ts` (`credentialHandleNotAppliedReason`, `notConnectedReason`). The four facts `lint-flow-credential-literals.test.ts:533-536` pins are still verbatim in the string. No verdict, `fix:` line or hint moves. Right.
- **Ratchet rows.** `integration-recipes.md` 2236 → 2523 and `SKILL.md` 6457 → 6454, both re-locked AT the measurement (re-measured below under ④). Right.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/28299-automation-skill-oauth-recipe.md`: `packages/skills` (name `objectstack/skills` scope, `files` ships `skills`) **patch** — text in a released package, no shape moves. Matches the diff.
- `.changeset/28299-lint-grant-steer-served.md`: `packages/lint` **patch** — an explanation string in a released package, a fix, not `skip-changeset`. Matches the diff.
- `Clause-②: no` in the PR body and both changesets. The lint changeset's `no (lint advice is not a contract face; …)` is well-formed: `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` reads the token first after the colon and accepts trailing reasoning; the parenthetical is not a `(widening)`/`(narrowing)` arm and is not read as one. `Metadata-protocol: none` on all three. Check Changeset is green. Levels and lines are right.

### ③ Boundary flags

The os-dev-report (comment 6553500238) carries `open_questions: []` and two `out_of_scope_findings`, both class "observation":

1. **"SKILL.md keeps 'request signing' in the loader-gap list … the words stay true."** Not accepted as written. The words are true for WeChat Pay and false for the three served schemes; the line is unqualified, and the claim's own file surface was "one shrink of the loader-gap line … only for gaps now served" — signing is served for three of four named vendors. Answered as should-fix S1 under ④.
2. **"recipe 6 names no Console Connect page: none on main (route ledger: ADR-0143 S4)."** Confirmed: `route-ledger.ts:573` says "NOT JS-SDK surface on this leg: the driver is the Console's Connect / Reconnect flow (ADR-0143 S4)" and nothing under `ui/` is in #28399/#28419/#28437. The recipe teaches the three HTTP calls the ledger serves, which is the right posture; agreed, no change.

The PR body's "Not changed, noted for the server lane: `credentialHandleNotAppliedReason` says a provider 'does not yet ask' the handle" — checked at `plugin.ts:472-473`; the reason text is reached only for a provider registered without `{ credentialHandle: true }`, where it is still true. No escalation.

The card's Wanted item 1 (the interim "no built-in provider takes the grant yet" wording) is overtaken by item 2; item 2's "run the skill's evals" — no root eval runner exists for `skills/**` (`check:skill-eval-tokens` is the `ui/` catalogue's), the dev validated the fixture as JSON; accepted, since the rubric is judged above.

### ④ Design judgment

**Recipe 6 against the spec and the code on `main`** (each statement, where it holds):

- "served on `rest`, `openapi` and `mcp`" — the three `credentialHandle: true` registrations cited in ①. Both `oauth2` grants and all three `app-credential` vendors reach the handle on all three providers; `plugin.ts` holds nothing degraded for the provider itself.
- "`mcp` (`http` only; a `stdio` server's credentials ride `transport.env`)" — `connector-mcp-plugin.ts:103-104` (an http transport asks the handle per request), `mcp-provider.ts:74` (not applied to stdio; a stdio server receives its env), connectors.mdx (a handle on a stdio transport fails the boot).
- "token fetched per dispatch, kept in memory, refreshed before expiry and once on a `401`; no metadata key holds it" — `grant-handle.ts:10` (refresh once on a `401`, retry once); connectors.mdx (30 s before expiry, in memory only); `connector-auth.zod.ts` `runtimeTokenGuidance` refuses `accessToken` / `refreshToken` / `token` by name.
- The `authorization_code` shape (`authorizationUrl`, `tokenUrl`, `scopes`, `clientId`, `credentialRef`; "PKCE always on"; "the ref is the client secret, omitted for a public client") — `ConnectorInstanceOAuth2AuthorizationCodeAuthSchema`: `credentialRef` optional with `dependentRequired({ credentialRef: ['clientId'] })`, `pkce` refused ("always uses PKCE with S256"). Holds.
- "`client_credentials` with `tokenUrl`, `clientId`, `credentialRef` (`resource` optional)" — `ConnectorInstanceOAuth2ClientCredentialsAuthSchema` (both-or-neither refine on `clientId`/`credentialRef`; `resource` optional, alias `audience`). Holds.
- `app-credential` shape (`vendor: 'feishu'`, `appId`, `credentialRef`) and the token placement "Feishu bearer, DingTalk `x-acs-dingtalk-access-token`, WeCom `access_token` query" — `app-credential.ts:128, 151, 178`. Holds.
- "`client_credentials` and `app-credential` dispatch once the ref is set" — neither has a connection state; `plugin.ts` degrades them only for a non-applying provider / insecure endpoint. Holds.
- "`authorization_code` is degraded 'not connected' until an administrator holding `manage_connector_connections` (organization admins by default) connects it, once per organization, from a signed-in session (an agent or API key is refused)" — `plugin.ts:2697` `notConnectedReason`; `default-permission-sets.ts:448` (org admin set carries the capability, record 6545223261); `domains/automation.ts:957-980` refuses `agent`, `oauth` and `api_key` callers by name ("a human administrator's act, taken from a signed-in session"). Holds.
- The three calls and the callback (`POST …/:name/connection` → `{ authorizationUrl }`, vendor redirect to `GET …/connectors/oauth/callback`, `GET` status `not_connected` / `connected` / `reconnect_required`, `DELETE` revokes) — `route-ledger.ts:572-579`. Holds.
- "Endpoints are `https://`" — `oauth2NotServableReason` (`isSecureOAuth2Endpoint`, `insecureOAuth2EndpointFields`; loopback exception omitted from the recipe, acceptable).
- "Still never park a short-lived token behind a `bearer` ref" — kept, as the card asked; still true (connectors.mdx's closing paragraph).
- Not named: a Console Connect page (none on `main`, ③ 2). DocuSign endpoints in the example are the vendor's real `account.docusign.com/oauth/auth` and `/oauth/token`; scope `signature` is a real DocuSign scope.

**Ratchet (ruling record 6513306068 / the 2026-10-27 standing ruling 「A:先削重复,余额按实测提高」), each condition on the tree:**

- *Deletion of restatement in the same file, shown in the diff* — two hunks in `integration-recipes.md`: (1) recipe 3's three-line `refresh_low_stock` / `ai: { exposed: true, … }` example → a one-line pointer; its home is `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` § Actions as AI Tools (L135 on `main`), which teaches `ai.exposed: true` + `ai.description` ≥ 40 chars on a `flow`-type action; nothing is lost. (2) "Each `operationId` is a named action in the flow palette and to agents;" — the Holds bullet already says "Actions come from the upstream (an OpenAPI `operationId`, …)"; the "flow palette" half has its home in connectors.mdx L22; the "to agents" half names nothing on `main` (no code in `service-ai` exposes connector actions to agents — only opted-in object actions are tools), so its deletion removes an unbacked claim, not a rule. **No rule lost its only home.** The `provider: 'rest'` half of the sentence stays.
- *No re-wrap to win room* — the diff touches only the two cut hunks, the replaced "Not yet" bullet/heading and the new section; no existing line is re-flowed.
- *PR body quotes the ruling* — it quotes record 6513306068 and the 2026-10-27 words verbatim, with the measured delta.
- *Pinned AT the measurement* — re-measured from the blobs: `integration-recipes.md` 8938 bytes on `main` (2235 tokens, headroom 1 under the 2236 row) → 10089 bytes on the head, ceil(10089/4) = **2523** = the new row. Partition re-derived from the blobs: cut 1 −236, cut 2 −72 (−308 together); recipe 6 block 1838 bytes less the 373-byte removed bullet and the 6-byte shorter heading = +1459; net +1151. Matches the row comment exactly. `SKILL.md`: 25836 bytes less the 20-byte stamp line (`  version: "18.2.0"` + newline, `pricedTokens` at `check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs:1034`) = 25816 → ceil = **6454** = the new row (a lowering, always legitimate). The row comments record the arithmetic in the form the header asks. No other row moves.
- *10402 principle (no growth for a small feature)* — +287 tokens turns a five-line "blocked" bullet into a served recipe spanning two grants, three vendors, a connect flow and its refusal; this is not a small feature and the shape-giving core (the two `auth` literals, the connect call, who may connect, the refusal, the `bearer`-ref warning) is what an author needs and is not taught elsewhere in `skills/**`. Part of it is restatement of connectors.mdx that gives an author nothing to write: named as should-fix S3 below.

**Findings:**

- **S1 (should-fix)** `SKILL.md` ≈L416: "request signing" stays unqualified in the loader-gap list while three `signed` schemes are served on `openapi` / `rest`. Say the gap as it is — WeChat Pay's (or "a signing scheme outside the three") — or drop the item and let the recipes file's "Not yet" carry it; dropping is a shrink on a row at headroom 0.
- **S2 (should-fix)** recipe 6: "on `mcp` they and `clientId` may be omitted, discovered at connect" — only an `authorization_code` instance discovers them (`plugin.ts` `oauth2NotServableReason`: "only an `authorization_code` instance on `provider: 'mcp'` over an http transport discovers them"), while the publish door (`connector.zod.ts` `isMcpHttpInstance`) lets a `client_credentials` mcp-http instance omit them too, so an author following the sentence literally gets a clean `os validate` and a degraded boot. Qualify with `authorization_code`.
- **S3 (should-fix)** proportion under 10402: three clauses restate connectors.mdx (already the file's header pointer) and declare nothing — the vendor token-placement parenthetical ("Feishu bearer, DingTalk `x-acs-dingtalk-access-token`, WeCom `access_token` query"), "kept in memory, refreshed before expiry and once on a `401`", and the `GET` status triple with its parenthetical. Roughly 70–80 tokens; cut and re-lock the row lower at the measurement.
- **S4 (should-fix, nit)** the surviving heading "Not yet — declare it, mark the integration blocked, write no plugin" now holds WeChat Pay alone, which cannot be declared (`ConnectorSigningSchemeSchema` is a closed enum); "declare it" is a leftover of "declare the rest". Also the Holds bullet's "`auth`, each variant with a `credentialRef`" lists four kinds and not the two recipe 6 serves — a pointer to recipe 6 there would keep the bullet true to its "each variant".

No must-fix. The recipe is one an AI author can follow on `main` today; nothing it promises is held degraded or unserved on `rest`, `openapi` or `mcp` (http), for either `oauth2` grant or any `app-credential` vendor.
